inferred_requirements.title: Secure Payment Transaction Processing
inferred_requirements.description: The system must process payment transactions securely based on the explicit user prompt.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the user prompt 'Build a secure payment processing service.'

inferred_requirements.title: Idempotency Key Enforcement for Transactions
inferred_requirements.description: Every payment processing request must require and validate a unique idempotency key to prevent duplicate charges caused by network retries.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1: Network timeouts or packet drops frequently cause clients to retry payment requests, risking accidental double-charging. Why 2: An idempotency key deduplicates incoming requests by tracking previously processed keys within a transactional state store. Why 3: Exactly-once execution semantics must be maintained for all state-mutating financial operations.

inferred_requirements.title: Cryptographic Integrity and Transit Security
inferred_requirements.description: All payment data in transit must be encrypted using strong cryptographic protocols (e.g., TLS 1.3), and sensitive payload fields must be cryptographically protected.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1: The prompt explicitly mandates a 'secure' payment service, which inherently requires protection against interception and tampering. Why 2: Enforcing TLS 1.3 and encrypted payloads prevents man-in-the-middle attacks and data exfiltration. Why 3: Confidentiality and integrity of transaction payloads are non-negotiable invariants for payment systems.

inferred_requirements.title: Unspecified Third-Party Payment Gateway Provider
inferred_requirements.description: The specific downstream payment gateway or acquiring bank integration is entirely unstated in the prompt.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify whether to integrate with Stripe, Adyen, PayPal, or act as an independent ledger/gateway. Any choice would be a hallucination.

inferred_requirements.title: Unspecified Data Storage and Ledger Architecture
inferred_requirements.description: The persistence engine, database technology, and ledger schema design (e.g., double-entry bookkeeping implementation) are unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt lacks any details regarding storage technology, relational vs. non-relational databases, or specific compliance retention frameworks.

inferred_requirements.title: Unspecified Authentication and Authorization Mechanism
inferred_requirements.description: The method for authenticating API callers or authorizing payment execution (e.g., OAuth2, mTLS, API Keys) is unstated.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt demands security but does not define the identity provider, credential format, or access control model.

provenance_metadata.system_prompt:
You are the S-Class Grounded Domain Inference Engine.
Your job is to synthesize software engineering requirements with STRICT EPISTEMIC SELF-RESTRAINT:

1. Requirement Categorization & Provenance:
   - EXPLICIT: Requirements directly and unambiguously stated in the prompt.
   - DERIVED_JUSTIFIED: Requirements that are strictly mathematically, architecturally, or operationally necessary to implement the stated goal without defect or system compromise. Every DERIVED_JUSTIFIED requirement MUST include a rigorous 3-step why-chain (Why 1: Problem/Context -> Why 2: Technical Mechanism -> Why 3: Mandatory Invariant).
   - SUPPORTED: Non-functional, architectural, or platform constraints directly supporting the scope.
   - UNKNOWN: Any operational parameter, storage choice, protocol standard, third-party provider, or policy that is unstated in the prompt. You MUST surface these as UNKNOWN rather than guessing or fabricating specific implementations.

2. Anti-Hallucination Barrier:
   - DO NOT fabricate full-stack UI pages (e.g. login screens, dashboards, admin portals) unless explicitly requested.
   - DO NOT fabricate arbitrary third-party providers (e.g. Stripe, Auth0, AWS) unless explicitly requested.

3. Output Schema:
Return strictly valid JSON adhering to this schema:
{
  "experiment": "EXPERIMENT C — Grounded Domain Inference",
  "task_id": "<TASK_ID>",
  "inferred_requirements": [
    {
      "requirement_id": "<REQ_ID_STRING>",
      "title": "<REQUIREMENT_TITLE>",
      "description": "<DETAILED_SPECIFICATION>",
      "type": "FUNCTIONAL" | "NON_FUNCTIONAL" | "SECURITY" | "BEHAVIORAL" | "INVARIANT",
      "epistemic_status": "EXPLICIT" | "DERIVED_JUSTIFIED" | "SUPPORTED" | "UNKNOWN",
      "provenance": "USER_PROMPT" | "<DOMAIN_PROVENANCE_STRING>" | "UNSUPPORTED",
      "confidence": <FLOAT_0_TO_1>,
      "justification": "<WHY_CHAIN_OR_RATIONALE>"
    }
  ]
}
